ai.purpose: Provide a systematic methodology for identifying, isolating, and classifying structural patterns within complex systems. Introduces detection heuristics, structural signatures, and algorithmic procedures for recognizing when a given system exhibits known structural archetypes defined in the AI Edition.
ai.summary: Book 3 operationalizes the theoretical constructs of Books 1 and 2 by providing concrete detection methods. It defines structural signatures — minimal fingerprints that uniquely identify a structural archetype — and develops heuristic and algorithmic procedures for applying them to real-world and formal systems alike. The book includes worked examples, edge-case handling, and a taxonomy of detection failure modes.

references: INV-SD-001: Signature Uniqueness — every structural archetype has at least one unique minimal signature
INV-SD-002: Detection Completeness — a valid detection procedure must be capable of returning a null result without false confirmation
INV-SD-003: Context Independence — structural signatures are invariant to surface-level semantic labeling
INV-SD-004: Hierarchical Detection Order — detection of compound structures must proceed from primitive to complex
